title: Add headless iasim serve startup for LAN testing
description:
Context: The open session lifecycle and LAN binding are complete, but the CLI still exits after logging instead of starting the MCP server. The operator needs a headless startup path now so they can run the LAN server and test external agents before the full GUI integration lands.

Scope: Add a `serve` command to the existing CLI. `iasim serve --headless` creates the GameSession/world, writes agents.json under the run directory, starts the authenticated MCP server on the configured host/port, prints the endpoint and LAN warning, and stays alive until Ctrl+C. Support --config, --host, --port, --max-agents, --seed, --log-dir, and the existing config flags. Without --headless, report that the GUI startup is not available yet and exit with the configuration error code; the full GUI remains iasim-qul.12.

SRS: RF-102, RF-104, RF-111, RF-110; docs/SRS.md sections 3.11, 6.1, and 7.2.

Non-goals: Full operator GUI, UI controls, full JSONL logs/metrics, TLS, transport disconnect/timeout handling, and F2/F3 features.
design: Add an optional positional `serve` command to the existing parser. Reuse the current config/seed/run-dir/logging path, construct GameSession with the configured max_agents and token_path, and call run_server with the configured host/port. run_server prints the advertised endpoint and warning. Keep the implementation separate from the full GUI; iasim-qul.12 will reuse the helper. Ctrl+C is treated as a clean shutdown.
acceptance_criteria: iasim serve --headless --config PATH --host H --port P --max-agents N --seed S --log-dir DIR creates the run directory and agents.json, starts the MCP server with auth and health, prints the endpoint and any LAN warning, and blocks until Ctrl+C/exit code 0. Without --headless it exits with a clear configuration error and does not start the server. Tokens never appear in logs or stdout. Tests cover parsing, headless startup with a patched server, config precedence, run artifacts, and the non-headless rejection; the manual LAN check is recorded in iasim-qul.6.
notes: The operator command is `iasim serve --headless --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765 --max-agents 8 --seed 42 --config config/iasim.toml`. Tokens remain in agents.json and are shared per slot. No GUI is opened by this slice.

title: Enable opt-in LAN MCP access with token distribution and warnings
description:
Context: The SRS now defines a server that is loopback-only by default but can be exposed explicitly on the local network so other people can connect their agents. The existing auth layer already issues per-slot bearer tokens, but the CLI, warning, connection instructions, and network tests are missing.

Scope: Add explicit host configuration and CLI (--host / mcp.host) while keeping 127.0.0.1 as the default. For non-loopback hosts, require token auth, show the LAN URL and a visible warning, reject --dev-open, keep agents.json restricted, and document trusted-LAN use. Cover config validation, binding, /healthz, and authenticated join tests.

SRS: RF-111, RF-1001, RF-1002, RNF-10; docs/SRS.md sections 6.1 and 7.2.

Non-goals: TLS, public Internet exposure, spectator UI, agent administration, and F2/F3 features.
design: Reuse McpConfig.host/port and uvicorn. Resolve the host from config or --host, validate that dev_open is loopback-only, derive the advertised URL from the bound host and port, and print the URL plus a warning without printing tokens. Keep tokens in the existing restricted agents.json and document sharing one token per slot. No TLS in the MVP; recommend a VPN or trusted LAN for anything beyond local testing.
acceptance_criteria: Loopback remains the default; --host 0.0.0.0 or a LAN IP binds the MCP server; an authenticated client can join from another host on the same network; missing or invalid tokens are rejected; --dev-open is rejected for non-loopback hosts; the LAN URL and security warning are visible; tokens never appear in logs; tests cover configuration, health, auth, and rejection paths.
notes: The operator starts the server with `iasim serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765 --max-agents 8` and shares the LAN URL plus one token per slot. The GUI is operator-only; remote clients are MCP agents and receive perception-limited observations.

title: Decide open LAN server with ephemeral agents and live operator GUI
description:
Context: The SRS currently specifies a lobby with a configured minimum, a five-second countdown, and agents that remain in the world as absent after transport loss. The product direction is an operator-started LAN server that generates the island, opens the operator GUI, and accepts up to eight concurrent MCP agents at any time. Agents exist only while their connection is open, are visible to the operator while connected, and leave JSONL records for later review.

Scope: Record the decision and update docs/SRS.md. Cover the open server lifecycle, agent connection/disconnect semantics, token/slot reuse, LAN binding and security, GUI monitoring, max concurrent agents, and logs. Re-scope affected Beads issues. Define defaults: loopback by default, explicit LAN host, token per slot, disconnect removes the agent and drops its inventory, death leaves a corpse, no agents pauses the simulation but keeps the server and GUI open, the operator ends the session, the GUI is operator-only, and headless remains available for tests.

Non-goals: Implementation code, spectator GUI for non-operators, TLS or public Internet exposure, and F2/F3 features.
design: The server and GUI share one GameSession; MCP runs in the background. The GUI is operator-only and sees the full world. Agents receive perception-limited observations and are bound to their MCP connection. LAN access is opt-in via --host, still requires bearer tokens, and warns about plaintext HTTP. Stable tokens are allocated per slot for the server lifetime; a disconnect frees the slot and the token can be reused for a new agent. The decision must be closed before dependent implementation issues start.
acceptance_criteria: SRS sections 3.2, 3.11, 4.1, 6.1, 7.1, 7.2, 8.1, 10, 11.2, 12, and 13 reflect the decision; affected issues have updated scope, acceptance criteria, and dependencies; no implementation code is changed.
notes: Default launch: iasim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765 --max-agents 8. LAN: --host 0.0.0.0 (or the LAN IP). --headless disables the GUI. Logs: events.jsonl, actions.jsonl, thoughts.jsonl, agents.json; never tokens in logs.

title: Add integrated iasim startup with LAN access and full operator GUI
description:
Context: The product GUI is the planned 160x45 operator interface, not a reduced monitor. The main command must launch that GUI together with the world and the MCP service. The same command must be highly parameterizable and accept a TOML configuration file whose values can be overridden by CLI flags.

Scope: Implement the main integrated command (`iasim`, with `iasim serve` and `python -m iasim` aliases). By default it creates the GameSession/world, opens the full planned GUI (map, tabbed right panel, agent strip, selected agent sheet, mind/events/connections, bottom bar), writes the run directory and agents.json, starts the authenticated MCP server, and keeps both alive. Add --config, --host, --port, --max-agents, --seed, --tick-minutes, --turn-timeout-ms, --timeout-disconnects, --snapshot-every, --autosave-every, --no-autosave, --log-dir, --dev-open, --load, --replay, and --headless. `--headless` is the only no-window variant. Print the URL and LAN warning; never print tokens.

SRS: RF-104, RF-107, RF-108, RF-111, RF-113; docs/SRS.md sections 3.11, 5.3, 5.5, 6.1, and 7.2.

Non-goals: F2/F3 views, TLS/public Internet exposure, spectator UI for non-operators, and unrelated refactors.
design: Create the orchestration around GameSession, create_app/run_server, the existing 160x45 renderer, the planned right-panel tabs and keyboard controls from sv5.*, and the log writers from 9i2.1. Run MCP in a background thread/task and the GUI loop in the main thread with a shared shutdown event. Resolve host, port, seed, run directory, and all gameplay/UI settings from TOML plus CLI overrides. Integrate the open lifecycle from 6kr.14, transport disconnect from 7a4.5, and LAN binding from 7a4.10. The GUI is operator-only and reads state without mutating it.
acceptance_criteria: The main command opens the full planned 160x45 GUI and starts the authenticated MCP server/world in one process; `iasim`, `iasim serve`, and `python -m iasim` behave identically; `--headless` starts only the MCP service; --config loads TOML and CLI flags override it; --host, --port, --max-agents, --seed, --tick-minutes, --turn-timeout-ms, --timeout-disconnects, --snapshot-every, --autosave-every, --no-autosave, --log-dir, --dev-open, --load, and --replay are honored; loopback is default and LAN use prints the URL plus a warning; agents.json and the run artifacts are created without tokens in logs; Ctrl+C/quit shuts down both; tests cover headless startup, health, auth, shutdown, config precedence, and a GUI render; the manual checklist covers the full windowed GUI and LAN path; SRS 7.2 documents the command.
notes: The full planned GUI is the default; do not ship a reduced monitor. --headless is only for tests and automation. The command must be usable as `iasim --config config/iasim.toml --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765 --max-agents 8`.

title: Implement open session lifecycle for ephemeral connected agents
description:
Context: The SRS now defines an operator-started server with the world and GUI visible from startup. There is no lobby, minimum agent count, or countdown. Agents exist only while their MCP connection is open, up to eight concurrent, and the server stays available when nobody is connected.

Scope: Replace the lobby lifecycle with an open session: accept joins between ticks up to max_agents; assign a free slot and spawn; expose session phase and connected/alive counts; remove an agent on graceful leave or disconnect, cancel its pending action, drop its inventory, and free its slot/token; keep corpses after death; pause when no agent is active; keep the server open after the last death; support operator finish/restart. The transport-level disconnect hook is implemented in iasim-7a4.5.

SRS: RF-104, RF-107, RF-108, RF-109, RF-112, RF-405; docs/SRS.md sections 3.2, 3.11, 4.1.

Non-goals: MCP transport detection, LAN binding, GUI integration, JSONL logs, and F2/F3 features.
design: Use an open lifecycle with explicit RUNNING/WAITING/FINISHED-style state and no countdown. Keep the session authoritative and thread-safe. Separate the application leave/remove operation from the MCP transport hook so iasim-7a4.5 can call it. Tokens are stable per slot for the server lifetime.
acceptance_criteria: The server starts with a valid world and no agents; the first join creates an agent at tick 0; up to eight agents can be connected; joins and leaves work between ticks; a disconnected agent is absent from the world, its pending action is cancelled, its inventory is on the ground, and its slot/token is reusable; no ghost agents remain; the simulation pauses when no agent is active; the server stays open after the last death; the operator can finish and restart; tests cover one agent, eight agents, disconnect, and slot reuse.
notes: The server and GUI remain open with the island visible when no agents are connected. No automatic session end on the last death or disconnect. The GUI reads the session state but never mutates it directly.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: open session lifecycle with 1-8 concurrent agents, between-tick joins, leave/inventory drop/token reuse, no lobby, operator finish/restart, session metadata, and tests; merged to main at 7d20a13; pytest 178 passed, 1 skipped; ruff/format/mypy clean.

title: Use the Beads CLI as the primary agent interface
description:
Context: Implements one coherent MVP slice of F0: Bootstrap project foundation and deterministic runtime. Work must follow AGENTS.md and the SRS.

Scope: Choose the default integration surface for agents: Beads CLI or the optional beads-mcp server.

SRS: SRS-11.1; see docs/SRS.md.

Non-goals: F2/F3 features, agent intelligence, MCP administration tools, and unrelated refactors.

## Decision
Use the Beads CLI as the primary interface for agents working in this repository.

## Rationale
The CLI is the upstream-recommended path for shell-capable agents, has much lower context overhead than MCP schemas, and is already available in this environment.

## Alternatives Considered
The optional beads-mcp server was considered. It remains available for MCP-only environments but is not required by this project, avoids an extra runtime dependency, and cannot be loaded into the current agent session.
acceptance_criteria: The decision is recorded; AGENTS.md mandates the CLI workflow; no MCP server dependency is introduced into the project runtime.
close_reason: CLI selected: upstream recommends it for shell-capable agents, it has lower context overhead, and beads-mcp remains optional.
